note: Satellites a handheld can actually work. Orbital elements in `tle` are refreshed daily by .github/workflows/tle.yml; everything else is hand-curated. Frequencies were taken from the SatNOGS transmitter database and then filtered by judgement, because that database tracks what a satellite has ever carried rather than what is worth tuning: it lists 29 transmitters for the ISS alone, including Soyuz suit channels and a 1990s Progress beacon. Satellites whose transmitters are dead are excluded even where the database still marks them alive - see `excluded` below.
excluded: NOAA 15, 18 and 19 (25338, 28654, 33591) carried the 137 MHz APT downlink that made weather satellites the classic beginner catch. All three were decommissioned in 2025 - NOAA 18 on 6 June, NOAA 19 passivated on 13 August, NOAA 15 on 19 August - and APT is no longer transmitted by anything. Celestrak still publishes their elements, so a tracker built on orbits alone would happily show passes for three silent satellites.
LAPAN-A2 (40931) has no current elements in Celestrak.
ESEO (43792), ICUBE-1 (39432), TISAT 1 (36799), XIWANG-1 (36122) and LilacSat-2 (40908) are listed as alive in SatNOGS but their missions have ended or their transponders are off.
Every telemetry beacon in BPSK, GMSK, LoRa and the like. They need a computer and a dish, not a handheld.

freqs.z: 国际空间站 —— 航天员语音
freqs.d: The downlink for scheduled school contacts and the occasional unscheduled chat. Silent most passes, and unmistakable when it is not: a 5 W transmitter 420 km up is louder than most repeaters on your local hilltop.
freqs.dz: 用于预约的校园通联，偶尔也有航天员随意聊天。多数过顶时段是安静的，但一旦有信号就绝不会听错 —— 420 公里高处的 5 瓦发射机，比本地山顶上多数中继台都响。

freqs.z: 国际空间站 —— APRS 数字中继
freqs.d: A packet digipeater that runs continuously, so this is the one ISS frequency that is almost always busy during a pass. You will hear bursts of data rather than voice.
freqs.dz: 常年开启的分组数字中继，因此这是国际空间站上过顶时几乎总有动静的频率。听到的是一阵阵数据声，而不是语音。

freqs.z: 国际空间站 —— 语音中继
freqs.d: A cross-band FM repeater: you transmit on 2 m and it comes back on 70 cm. Uplink needs a 67.0 Hz tone. Also the SSTV downlink when an image event is running.
freqs.dz: 跨波段 FM 中继：你用 2 米发射，它在 70 厘米返回。上行需要 67.0 Hz 亚音。图像活动期间，慢扫描电视（SSTV）也用这个频率下行。

freqs.z: 天宫空间站 —— 航天员语音
freqs.d: The Chinese station's 2 m crew channel, and the downlink used for its SSTV image events.
freqs.dz: 中国空间站的 2 米航天员话音频率，慢扫描电视图像活动时也用它下行。

freqs.z: 天宫空间站 —— FM 中继
freqs.d: The station's amateur repeater downlink. Activated for events rather than left running.
freqs.dz: 空间站业余中继的下行频率。按活动开启，不是长期开着。

freqs.d: The most dependable FM bird there is, and the one to try first. A 5 W handheld and a small directional antenna is genuinely enough. The uplink needs a 67.0 Hz tone to arm a 10-minute timer, so you may hear it come alive mid-pass when someone else arms it.
freqs.dz: 目前最可靠的 FM 卫星，建议第一个尝试。5 瓦手台加一副小型定向天线确实够用。上行需要 67.0 Hz 亚音来启动 10 分钟计时器，所以你可能会听到它在过顶途中被别人激活。

freqs.d: Nine Israeli school satellites flying in a string, all sharing one downlink. Because they are spread around the same orbit, one of them is overhead far more often than any single satellite would be.
freqs.dz: 九颗以色列校园卫星排成一串，共用同一个下行频率。由于它们分布在同一轨道上，头顶有一颗的机会远高于任何单颗卫星。

freqs.d: Still up and still usable, but the batteries have aged: it now works only while in sunlight, so a pass in the Earth's shadow gives you nothing.
freqs.dz: 仍在轨、仍可用，但电池已老化：现在只在阳照区工作，因此在地影中的过顶什么也收不到。

freqs.d: One of the oldest amateur FM birds flying. Runs on a schedule rather than continuously, and shares its downlink with SO-50, so check which one is actually overhead.
freqs.dz: 在轨最老的业余 FM 卫星之一。按时间表开机而非长期开启，且与 SO-50 共用下行频率，所以要确认头顶到底是哪一颗。

freqs.d: A Philippine satellite whose repeater is switched on for announced windows, usually over Asia and the Pacific.
freqs.dz: 菲律宾的卫星，中继只在公告的时段开启，通常覆盖亚洲和太平洋区域。

freqs.z: 金牛座一号 —— FM 中继
freqs.d: A Chinese amateur payload with a 70 cm FM downlink, worth a listen on any pass over Asia.
freqs.dz: 中国的业余载荷，70 厘米 FM 下行，亚洲上空的过顶都值得一听。

freqs.d: Kuwait's amateur satellite. Also carries an SSTV downlink on the same frequency.
freqs.dz: 科威特的业余卫星。同一频率上还有慢扫描电视下行。

freqs.z: 中俄工大一号 —— FM 中继
freqs.d: A recent Chinese-Russian university satellite carrying an FM transponder and a camera.
freqs.dz: 较新的中俄高校合作卫星，带 FM 转发器和相机。

freqs.z: 流星 M2-3 —— 气象图像
freqs.d: Russian weather satellites still broadcasting images, but in digital LRPT rather than the analogue APT that NOAA used. A handheld hears the carrier and a harsh buzz; turning it into a picture needs a computer. Listed because it is the only weather imagery left in the 137 MHz band now that APT has ended.
freqs.dz: 俄罗斯气象卫星仍在广播图像，但用的是数字 LRPT，而不是 NOAA 曾用的模拟 APT。手台能听到载波和刺耳的杂音，要还原成图像需要电脑。收录它，是因为 APT 停播之后，137 MHz 段只剩下这一种气象图像。

freqs.z: 流星 M2-4 —— 气象图像
freqs.d: The newer of the pair, on the same downlink. Both are in the same sun-synchronous orbit, so their passes come at similar times of day.
freqs.dz: 两颗中较新的一颗，下行频率相同。二者在同一太阳同步轨道上，因此过顶时间也相近。
